trap-trigger.text: a flagstone that sits a finger's width proud of the rest

trap-trigger: a tripwire of blackened gut, ankle-high across a doorway
lifting the lid of a chest
the third step of a stair, and only the third
a door handle turned the wrong way
a torch bracket that pulls down like a lever
too much weight on a bridge or landing
a loose tile in a mosaic, pressed by anyone admiring it
light falling on a mirrored plate in the ceiling
taking the obvious prize from its plinth
a hidden latch on the inside of a cupboard
a rope pulled from the far end, by someone watching
opening a door while the one behind is still open
breaking a wax seal across a doorway
the warmth of a living body crossing a threshold
a book drawn halfway out of its shelf
stepping on the shadow cast by a statue at noon

trap-trigger.text: a word spoken anywhere in the room, in any language

trap-effect.text: a section of floor drops into a {10-40}-foot pit, its sides greased
a fan of darts from slots in the wall, their tips tacky with something
a heavy grate slams down, splitting the party in two
the room's exits seal and water begins to pour in from the ceiling
a counterweighted log swings down the length of the corridor
a jet of burning oil from a lion's-head spout
a net of weighted chain drops from the ceiling, loud enough to wake the whole level
the floor tilts, and everything on it slides toward a chute
a cloud of fine yellow dust that sets everyone coughing and weeping
a blade sweeps out at knee height from a slot in the wall
the ceiling lowers, slowly but steadily, on a groaning chain
a bell rings somewhere deep below, and keeps ringing
the door behind locks, and the one ahead now opens onto a sheer drop
a needle springs from the lock, and the hand that touched it goes numb to the elbow
every lamp in the room goes out, and the floor begins, very slowly, to turn
loose masonry rains down from a section of ceiling built to collapse
a pane of thin glass shatters, releasing a swarm of furious hornets
a cage drops over whoever stands on the dais
the stair flattens into a smooth stone ramp
a gout of freezing mist that rimes everything it touches
{a} {metal} plate in the floor crackles with stored lightning
a hidden bellows fills the room with smoke, and something starts moving in it

trap-tell: a faint draught from a crack that should not be there
scratches on the floor in a neat arc
a clean patch in an otherwise filthy corridor
a scattering of old bones, all on one side of the room
a smell of lamp oil where there are no lamps
a tiny hole at waist height in each wall
dust that has been disturbed only in the middle of the floor
{a} {color} chalk mark at shoulder height, left by someone who came before
a hum, felt more than heard, through the soles of the feet
a corpse still holding a ten-foot pole
fresh oil on a hinge in a ruin otherwise rusted solid
a warning scratched into the plaster, then carefully scratched out

trap-tell.text: no sign at all — whoever built it knew their trade

trap-disarm: jam the mechanism with a spike before anyone crosses
cut the linkage — but slacken it first, or it fires anyway
find the counterweight room above and jam the chain
pour sand into the slots until the mechanism chokes
trigger it deliberately from a safe distance
hold the trigger down the whole time someone passes
replace the prize with something of equal weight
the builder's own safe word, if anyone can find it
a hidden bypass lever behind the third brick from the left
it cannot be disarmed, only outrun
disable it from the other side, which means someone has to get there first
wait: it resets on a timer, and there is a gap
trap-twist: it has been disarmed already — badly
it is a decoy; the real trap is the safe-looking way round
triggering it also opens a secret door
something lives in the pit, and has been well fed
the builder is still alive, and still listening for it
the mechanism is so old that it fires a moment too late
it was built to keep something in, not to keep anyone out
it resets itself, and the second time is worse
a previous victim is still caught in it, and still alive
it is linked to every other trap on the level
trap-maker: a paranoid wizard who never let anyone else into the workshop
kobold tinkerers who take great pride in their work
a guild of thieves, guarding their own hoard
a dead king's engineers, who were sealed in afterwards
a clockmaker who considered it art
the current tenants, quickly and with whatever was to hand
no one knows; it is older than the rest of the place

natural-hazard.text: a hillside of loose scree that shifts with every step
a sudden fog bank that rolls in off the water and does not lift
a peat bog that looks exactly like a meadow
a river in spate, carrying whole trees down with it
a lightning storm with the party as the tallest thing for miles
ice over moving water, thinner than it looks in the middle
snow cornices along a ridge, overhanging nothing
a whiteout that turns the world into one blank page
a stand of trees so dry that one spark would take the whole valley
a wildfire on the wind, a mile off and closing
a cave passage that floods to the roof when it rains outside
bad air pooled in a low tunnel — candles gutter, then go out
a sinkhole opening under the road with a long, soft sigh
a hornets' nest the size of a barrel in a hollow log
a stretch of sand that drinks anyone who stands still
a tide that comes in faster than a person can run
heat that shimmers off the rocks and empties water-skins by noon
a dust storm that strips paint and skin alike
an avalanche, set off by a careless shout
brambles thick enough to stop a horse, and sharp enough to stop the rider
a natural spring whose water tastes fine and causes a raging fever
a cliff path that has crumbled away in the night
a cloud of biting flies so thick it darkens the sun
a hot spring field where the crust over the boiling mud is very thin
a cave ceiling covered in sleeping bats, all of them very easily woken

hazard: {natural-hazard} — and {a} {creature} is caught in it, panicking
